sentence.text: Over 2027–2031, Pennsylvania would likely permit between 1,200 and 5,100 more homes (1.2–3.5%) with parking minimums removed, on top of a baseline of 67,000–180,000 homes expected under today's rules.

label.text: Baseline: homes permitted under today's rules
Homes added by the reforms
Change from the baseline

why.text: Middle estimate: 2.1% more homes than the baseline. “Adds some” means 1% to under 5%.

label.text: Transit-rich tracts

meaning.text: Neighbourhoods with frequent transit nearby.

steps.formula: transit-rich tracts = 814 of 3445 (at least half of the tract's homes within 1/2 mile of rail or 1/4 mile of a bus stop with 64+ weekday departures, or a major stop inside the tract)

label.text: Spaces required per unit before the reform

meaning.text: Parking spaces the rules require for each new home today.

steps.formula: spaces required per unit, baseline-weighted over counties and 2-, 3-4- and 5+-unit buildings = 1.55 spaces/unit

label.text: Spaces still built per unit after the reform

meaning.text: Parking spaces builders would still choose to build without a rule.

steps.formula: spaces still built per unit = required x share still built (transit-rich 0.6, elsewhere 0.925), weighted by the transit-rich share of each county's homes = 1.11 spaces/unit

label.text: Spaces avoided per unit

meaning.text: Spaces no longer built for each new home.

steps.formula: spaces required per unit before the reform (baseline-weighted) (1.55 spaces/unit) − spaces still built per unit after the reform (baseline-weighted) (1.11 spaces/unit) = 0.442 spaces/unit

label.text: Cost per space avoided

meaning.text: What each space not built would have cost.

steps.formula: cost per space avoided = average saving / average spaces avoided, from the surface, structured and underground mix of each tract class

label.text: Parking saving per unit

meaning.text: The saving on each new home from building fewer spaces.

steps.formula: spaces avoided per unit (0.442 spaces/unit) × cost per space avoided (baseline-weighted mix) ($27,440/space) = $12,120/unit

label.text: Baseline units 2027-2031, building types reached

meaning.text: Homes the baseline expects to be permitted in the building types this reform reaches.

steps.formula: baseline units 2027-2031 in the building types this reform reaches = 63,412 units (projected from building permits)

label.text: Value per new unit

meaning.text: What a typical new home is worth, so the saving can be compared with it.

steps.formula: value per new unit, effective = average saving / baseline-weighted average of (saving / value) over counties and building types = $220,187/unit (county medians from ACS brackets x (1 + new-construction premium); rented types capitalised at the cap rate)

label.text: Saving as a share of value

meaning.text: The saving as a share of a new home's value: the size of the push to build.

steps.formula: parking saving per unit ($12,120/unit) ÷ value per new unit (effective) ($220,187/unit) = 0.055

label.text: Medium-run supply response to a change in profit per unit

meaning.text: How strongly builders respond when building becomes more profitable.

steps.formula: Medium-run supply response to a change in profit per unit = 1 (ledger supply.elasticity_medium_run, central)

label.text: Share of a cost saving that reaches the decision to build

meaning.text: How much of the saving reaches the decision to build, rather than land prices.

steps.formula: Share of a cost saving that reaches the decision to build = 0.5 (ledger supply.saving_passthrough_k, central)

label.text: Added units from the parking cost saving, central values

meaning.text: Extra homes because each home costs less to build, at central values.

steps.formula: baseline units 2027-2031, building types reached (63,412 units) × Medium-run supply response to a change in profit per unit (1) × saving as a share of value (0.055) × Share of a cost saving that reaches the decision to build (0.5) = 1,745 units

label.text: Added units from site yield, central values

meaning.text: Extra homes because land once kept for parking can hold homes, at central values.

steps.formula: baseline units x site-yield gain (0.05) x share of spaces avoided, summed = 902.5 units

label.text: Added units from parking reform, central values

meaning.text: Both parking effects together, at central values.

steps.formula: added units from the parking cost saving, central values (1,745 units) + added units from site yield, central values (902.5 units) = 2,648 units

label.text: Homes added, likely range

meaning.text: The same chain worked out in every simulated draw, with every uncertain input varied together.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over counties of added units per county in each draw; per draw: baseline units x e x (spaces avoided x cost per space / value per new unit) x k + baseline units x site-yield gain x share of spaces avoided, summed over counties and structure types in each draw = 1,242 units, 2,651 units, 5,088 units

general.title: What these estimates cannot tell you

items.text: These are likely ranges of building permits, not a forecast of homes finished.
They describe the whole state. They do not say which lots, streets or owners would build.
They do not say who would live in the new homes or what they would pay.
They assume every town follows the new rule from the first day and approves permits at today's pace.
They say nothing about years after the five-year period.
The baseline repeats recent permit trends under today's rules. It does not predict a recession or a boom.
Counties without a permit office, or with imputed permit counts, carry the Census Bureau's estimates.
Whether lenders in a given market would finance buildings with fewer spaces.
Effects on street parking and on neighbours.
Whether land freed from parking becomes homes or something else.
Savings on townhouses, which the permit data count together with detached homes.

title.text: How many more homes would Pennsylvania permit?

label.text: More homes permitted with the reforms
Baseline: homes permitted under today's rules
With the reforms

body.text: Over 2027–2031, Pennsylvania would likely permit between 1,200 and 5,100 more homes (1.2–3.5%) with parking minimums removed, on top of a baseline of 67,000–180,000 homes expected under today's rules.
Decision support, not a forecast. Not an official state document.

label.text: More homes permitted, this reform alone
Baseline units 2027-2031, building types reached

meaning.text: Homes the baseline expects to be permitted in the building types this reform reaches.

items.formula: baseline units 2027-2031 in the building types this reform reaches = 63,412 units (projected from building permits)

label.text: Added units from the parking cost saving, central values

meaning.text: Extra homes because each home costs less to build, at central values.

items.formula: baseline units 2027-2031, building types reached (63,412 units) × Medium-run supply response to a change in profit per unit (1) × saving as a share of value (0.055) × Share of a cost saving that reaches the decision to build (0.5) = 1,745 units

label.text: Added units from site yield, central values

meaning.text: Extra homes because land once kept for parking can hold homes, at central values.

items.formula: baseline units x site-yield gain (0.05) x share of spaces avoided, summed = 902.5 units

label.text: Added units from parking reform, central values

meaning.text: Both parking effects together, at central values.

items.formula: added units from the parking cost saving, central values (1,745 units) + added units from site yield, central values (902.5 units) = 2,648 units

label.text: Homes added, likely range

meaning.text: The same chain worked out in every simulated draw, with every uncertain input varied together.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over counties of added units per county in each draw; per draw: baseline units x e x (spaces avoided x cost per space / value per new unit) x k + baseline units x site-yield gain x share of spaces avoided, summed over counties and structure types in each draw = 1,242 units, 2,651 units, 5,088 units

body.text: Middle estimate: 2.1% more homes than the baseline. “Adds some” means 1% to under 5%.
Homes the baseline expects to be permitted in the building types this reform reaches.

title.text: What these estimates cannot tell you

label.text: More homes permitted with the reforms

body.text: These are likely ranges of building permits, not a forecast of homes finished.
They describe the whole state. They do not say which lots, streets or owners would build.
They do not say who would live in the new homes or what they would pay.
They assume every town follows the new rule from the first day and approves permits at today's pace.
They say nothing about years after the five-year period.
Decision support, not a forecast. Not an official state document.
